defect: A --child argument alone previously admitted the probe body even on the input desktop.
reproduction: Two actual subprocesses on the input desktop, with and without redirected stderr, entered the sentinel body; both expected-rejection tests failed. Private desktop control passed.
fix: At is_child entry, read thread/input desktop names through Win32 APIs. Record names when an output directory is supplied; reject equal names and propagate API errors. Close the opened input-desktop handle in finally. No desktop switch or input injection.
scope: Windows native-probe helper, not application functionality. Same public signatures and no Qt construction in probes.
status: 755 source/test files frozen; full regression queued and incomplete.
limits: Entry check is not continuous monitoring. A child could later change desktops or issue forbidden input; probe code still requires review.
No claim that earlier foreground/cursor mismatches were caused by --child misuse. Those observations remain unresolved.
Actual tests cover same-desktop refusal and private-desktop admission; unavailable Win32 API paths were not induced.
Three tests require Windows desktops and skip on other platforms.
Independent review and full product integration remain incomplete. No EXE, push, merge or release.
